rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a balanced multimodal configuration using scvi_n200 (RNA) and imagenet_vit_l (image) encoders with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, which are promising choices for cellular profiling. This configuration clarifies the effectiveness of combining advanced image processing (ViT) with a strong RNA encoder. It is the best use of the budget as it explores a high-impact design choice (ViT) while maintaining reasonable cost compared to transformer-based alternatives.

The existing evidence shows that config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.706 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (a simpler, cheaper model) while keeping other components the same. It clarifies whether the choice of image encoder significantly impacts accuracy. Resnet50 is expected to have lower training cost (~3.5-4 GPU hours) than ViT, allowing more experiments within the budget while exploring a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.706 accuracy at 4.82 GPU hours. This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (config_041), which could improve performance by capturing complex interactions between modalities. While transformer is more expensive (~5.5 GPU hours), it's a logical extension of the promising multimodal/multiprofile setup. This balances exploitation of current success with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation method).

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with vit_l image encoder (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (which is less complex) to see if it maintains high accuracy with lower cost. The expected cost is similar to config_041 but potentially lower, balancing exploration and exploitation while keeping GPU hours low.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while keeping other components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) the same, to assess if this change improves accuracy. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choices on performance. The expected cost is similar to config_041 (3.60 GPU hours), balancing exploration of RNA encoder variations with cost efficiency.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_041: 0.725 accuracy) is strong, but the fusion method's impact remains unclear. This experiment tests the same RNA (scvi_n200) and image (imagenet_vit_l) encoders as the top performer but with concat fusion instead of weighted, clarifying if fusion type affects performance. It balances exploitation (building on top config) and exploration (testing fusion variation) with a similar cost (expected ~3.60 GPU hours) to the top performer.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (e.g., config_041: 72.5%). This experiment tests combining pca_n2000 RNA encoder (which may capture different features) with resnet50 image encoder (cheaper than ViT) under the same effective setup. It clarifies if encoder diversity improves accuracy while maintaining cost efficiency. Expected cost ~5.5 GPU hours, balancing exploration of encoder combinations with exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_041, 0.725 accuracy) is strong, but RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs. scgpt) remains uncertain. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same high-performing transformer + weighted setup, clarifying if RNA encoder choice impacts accuracy. It is low-cost (estimated ~3.6 GPU hours) and directly extends the top-performing configuration, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows config_041 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.725 accuracy with low cost (3.60 GPU hours), while config_025 (concat fusion) has slightly lower accuracy (0.720) but higher cost (4.65). This experiment tests whether using resnet50 image encoder (vs. imagenet_vit_l) with transformer aggregation and concat fusion could improve performance while maintaining cost efficiency. It clarifies if image encoder choice impacts accuracy when using transformer aggregation, and balances exploration of image encoder alternatives with the current top-performing architecture.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_041: 0.725). This experiment tests a new RNA encoder (scgpt) and image encoder (resnet50) with the same transformer+weighted setup, which could potentially improve accuracy. It balances exploration (testing new encoders) with exploitation (using proven aggregation/fusion). Estimated cost is ~5.5 GPU hours, which is reasonable given the remaining budget.
